title: The Langevin-equation description of optomechanics with the dispersive and dissipative optomechanical coupling
abstract: The description of the optomechanical system is commonly based on the quantum Langevin equation formalism. This framework is introduced phenomenologically or based on a model Hamiltonian. However, once dealing with the optomechanical Fabry-Perot cavity or the modified Michelson-Sagnac interferometer with a semitransparent mechanically active membrane inside, a model-free consideration is also possible by using an alternative approach. Such an approach, which is based on the classical wave equations in the systems, is popular in the gravitational-wave community where it is termed as input-output relations approach. In this work, using the aforementioned approach, we derived the equations for the ladder operator of the intracavity field, stochastic back-action force, and the relation between the fields at the input mirror. Then we simplified the obtained results down to the range of applicability of the Langevin equation formalism and compared these with the corresponding predictions of the latter formalism. This enabled us to critically assess the validity of the Langevin equation formalism and rectify its range of applicability. In the case where the dissipative optomechanical coupling is involved we identified appreciable problems with this formalism. We found that, disregarding the fact that decay rate of the optomechanical Fabry-Perot cavity depends on its length, no dissipative optomechanical coupling is generated. This is in contrast with the prediction of the standard Langevin-equation based treatment. We found that, staying inside the range of applicability of the Langevin equation formalism, the relation between the fields at the input mirror may not be correct. We found that the Langevin equation formalism misses a phase factor at the input field, this factor turns out to be important for the situation involving the dissipative optomechanical coupling.
summary: The paper compares the Input-Output (IO) approach with the Quantum Langevin equation formalism for optomechanical systems. It finds that while both methods describe dispersive coupling, the standard Langevin treatment incorrectly predicts dissipative coupling when decay rates depend on mechanical position. The authors conclude that a model-free IO analysis is necessary to correctly account for phase factors and the true physical origin of dissipation in these quantum optical setups.
main_problem: To critically assess the validity and range of applicability of the quantum Langevin equation formalism for describing optomechanical systems, especially when dissipative coupling is present.
main_result: The Input-Output (IO) approach reveals that standard Langevin formalisms incorrectly predict the generation of dissipative optomechanical coupling when only cavity decay rate dependence on length is considered. Furthermore, L-formalism may miss a crucial phase factor when dissipative coupling is active.
method: The authors compare results derived from the model-free Input-Output (IO) relations approach (based on classical wave equations) against those obtained using the standard quantum Langevin equation formalism for various cavity setups.
model_or_system: The study focuses on optomechanical systems, specifically utilizing an optomechanical Fabry-Perot cavity and a modified Michelson-Sagnac interferometer where one mirror acts as a mechanical oscillator. The comparison involves analyzing coupling mechanisms (dispersive vs. dissipative).
key_observables: Intracavity field ladder operator, stochastic back-action force spectral power density S(Omega), and the relation between input/output fields.
important_parameters: Dissipative optomechanical coupling strength ($g_\gamma$), cavity decay rate ($\gamma$), mechanical oscillator position dependence of $\gamma$, and phase factors.
main_assumptions: The comparison relies on simplifying the IO-approach results to match the structure of the Langevin formalism, though discrepancies are found when dissipative effects are included.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the problem by comparing L-formalism and IO-formalism. It then details the application of both formalisms to specific cavities (Fabry-Perot, MMSI), deriving equations for field operators and backaction forces in each framework before drawing comparative conclusions regarding dissipative coupling.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical check on established methods in quantum optics, highlighting where simplified or model-dependent approaches (like standard L-formalism) break down when moving to more complex physical regimes involving dissipation.
